mark_split.label: Read it as a scalar triple product
State the value and what it means

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.73, chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Short Answer question 33. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+2+1 split gives the first mark to reading the expression correctly — the cross product binds before the dot, so this is the scalar triple product [a b c] — half the marks to the determinant, and the last mark to stating a number rather than a vector. CHECKED TWO WAYS: expanding the single 3 × 3 determinant with rows (1, −2, 3), (2, 1, −1) and (0, 1, 1) gives 1(1 + 1) + 2(2) + 3(2) = 12; and computing the cross product first gives a × b = −i + 7j + 5k, which dotted with a = (1, −2, 3) gives −1 − 14 + 15 = 0 and dotted with b = (2, 1, −1) gives −2 + 7 − 5 = 0, so it is perpendicular to both, and dotting it with c = (0, 1, 1) gives 0 + 7 + 5 = 12, the same value. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, each worth 4 marks, under the 2026-27 pattern; Product of Vectors supplies at least one of those eight on almost every paper. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would simplify this — say which product is done first and whether the answer is a number or a vector.

steps.label: Read it as a scalar triple product
steps.margin_note: First mark. The cross product must come first, because a dot product gives a number and a number cannot be crossed with a vector. So the expression is [a b c].
steps.memory_tip: Cross before dot — the other order is not even defined, since a number cannot be crossed with a vector.
lines: Let a = i − 2j + 3k, b = 2i + j − k
The cross product is taken first, so
the expression is (a × b)·c = [a b c].

recall.must_convey: That the cross product is done first, so the expression is the scalar triple product [a b c].
accept: the cross comes first so this is the scalar triple product
it is a cross b dotted with c which is the box product
a dot product gives a number so the cross must come first
cross product modata, adi scalar triple product avutundi
read it as the box product a b c

steps.why: A dot product returns a number, and a number cannot be crossed with a vector, so only one reading of the expression makes sense. That reading is the scalar triple product, which is a single 3 × 3 determinant.
common_mistakes: Doing the dot product first, which leaves a number crossed with a vector.
Expecting a vector answer from a scalar triple product.

steps.label: Expand the 3 × 3 determinant
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. The rows are the components of a, b and c in the order the product names them. Write the zero component of c before starting.
steps.memory_tip: Rows go in the order the product names them: a, then b, then c. Swapping any two rows changes the sign.

recall.must_convey: That the determinant with rows (1, −2, 3), (2, 1, −1), (0, 1, 1) expands to 2 + 4 + 6 = 12.
accept: expand the determinant to get two plus four plus six
the three by three determinant works out to twelve
rows are the components of a then b then c
determinant expand cheste two plus four plus six equals twelve
one into two plus two into two plus three into two
reject: so the vectors are not coplanar

steps.why: The scalar triple product is the determinant of the nine components, taken in the order the product names the vectors. Row order is not free: swapping any two rows reverses the sign of the answer.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the zero i component of j + k.
Dropping the minus in front of the second term of the expansion.

steps.label: State the value
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The answer is a plain number, not a vector. It is non-zero, so the three vectors do not lie in one plane.
steps.memory_tip: A scalar triple product is a number, and a non-zero value means the three vectors are not coplanar.
lines: The value is a number, not a vector.
It is not zero, so a, b and c are not
coplanar; 12 is the volume, in cubic
units, of the box they span.

recall.must_convey: That the value is 12, a number, and that being non-zero means a, b and c are not coplanar.
accept: the answer is twelve, a number not a vector
since it is not zero the three vectors are not coplanar
twelve is the volume of the parallelepiped they span

steps.why: A scalar triple product is the signed volume of the box with a, b and c as edges. A value of 12 therefore says the volume is 12 cubic units and the three vectors do not lie in one plane.
common_mistakes: Writing the answer as 12i or as some other vector.
Reporting −12 by taking the rows in a different order.
